ashby:apex-technology-inc:f909dca4-a74a-.summary:
Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

sections.title: Operating Principles
paras: Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
bullets: Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

sections.title: AI-First by Default
paras: We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.
bullets: Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

ashby:delinea:b0d82a51-4494-4928-840a-78.summary:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: You will shape how Delinea helps organizations secure identities and control who can do what across their environments. You'll own the product strategy for authorization and privileged access: determining who gets access to which resources, under what conditions, and with what oversight. Your work will help customers reduce identity-based risk, enforce least privilege, and prove compliance, while keeping authorization decisions consistent, explainable, and practical for the people who rely on them every day. You'll set the vision and work directly with customers, partners, and internal teams to bring it to life.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Engage directly with customers, including security architects, CISOs, IAM administrators, and auditors, to understand their authorization and identity security challenges and validate solutions that reduce risk without slowing the business down.
Define and communicate a product vision for authorization that aligns with the evolving threat landscape and the growth of machine and non-human identities.
Drive capabilities for fine-grained, context-aware authorization, including attribute-based, and policy-based access models, so access decisions reflect identity, risk, and context.
Strengthen least privilege, zero trust, and just-in-time access, along with the approval workflows, visibility and audit evidence needed to show why access was granted, by whom, and for how long.
Partner closely with engineering, design, architecture and the GTM teams from problem definition through launch.
Track emerging trends in authorization, privileged access management, and regulatory requirements, and bring the best ideas back into the roadmap.

sections.title: Skills & Requirements
bullets: Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, business, or a similar field preferred.
5+ years of customer-facing product management experience, ideally in identity security, authorization, privileged access management (PAM) or the broader cybersecurity space.
Strong understanding of core identity security and authorization concepts: least privilege, zero trust, separation of duties, RBAC/ABAC/PBAC.
Familiarity with externalized authorization and policy-based access control approaches (e.g. OPA, Cedar) is highly desirable.
Working knowledge of public cloud environments (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform) and the authorization and access challenges they introduce.
Track record of successfully bringing security products or capabilities to market and driving customer adoption.
Experience with workflow automation or orchestration concepts is a plus.
Experience with API-first design and enterprise integrations is a plus.

sections.title: Why work at Delinea?
bullets: We're passionate problem-solvers helping the world's largest organizations protect what matters most: their human and machine identities.
We invest in people who are smart, self-motivated, and collaborative.
What we offer in return is meaningful work, a culture of innovation and great career progression.

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: The console is where every service Lambda sells meets the human user at the customer. It is the place where disparate products can come together to create a unified experience that solves a customer problem. Conversely, it is also the place where a cloud most easily becomes hard to use, because each service is built by a different team at a different time, and every one of them arrives with its own idea of what a resource is called, where it lives, who is allowed to touch it, and what a customer should do next. The customer does not experience a portfolio of services. They experience one product, and they judge us on whether it holds together.

This role owns that product. You own the console as a single surface, with one navigation model, one identity and permissions story, one set of interaction patterns, and one vocabulary, across On-Demand GPU Instances, reserved capacity, 1-Click Clusters, bare metal, storage, networking, Managed Kubernetes, billing, and support. Every service team ships into that surface, and the standards are yours to set. Your job is to make the whole thing feel like it was designed on purpose, which means writing the standards down, reviewing the work against them, and being the person who says no when a service wants to solve a problem in a way that only makes sense from inside that team.

Three very different people have to succeed here. A machine learning researcher wants a graphics processing unit (GPU) in minutes and should never have to learn cloud vocabulary to get one. An infrastructure engineer runs large clusters, lives in the application programming interface (API) and the command line, and needs the console to agree exactly with both. A platform engineer is building their own service on top of Lambda for their own users, and needs the console to make clear what their teams can see, spend, and change. The hard part of the role is that these three pull in different directions, and the surface cannot be quietly bent toward whichever one showed up in the last customer meeting.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the Whole Surface: Hold the product definition for the console as one product, decide what belongs in it and what does not, rank and sequence the work, and be honest about what Lambda is not doing this year and why.

Set the Patterns and Hold Them: Define the navigation, identity, permissions presentation, resource naming, states, errors, and empty screens that every service uses, write them down clearly enough that a team can build to them without asking you, then establish and run the review that console work passes before it ships.

Keep the Console Honest With the API: Make sure the console, the API, the command line, and infrastructure as code describe the same resources with the same names and the same rules, and treat a console-only capability as a problem to be fixed rather than a feature.
Find the Real Problem: Get close to customers, support tickets, escalations, and session data, and work out what is actually blocking people rather than what they asked for.
Write the Definition: Produce requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria precise enough that engineering and design build from them without a translation layer.
Work as a Group: Partner with the product managers who own each service so their launches land inside your surface as one product, and agree the seams early rather than at launch review.
Land the Launch: Set launch criteria that include documentation, in-product guidance, support readiness, and accessibility, and get them met before the surface goes live rather than after.

Drive capability maturity: Establish expectations for progressing capabilities from research or prototype stages through validation, productization, and production deployment.

Partner deeply with technical teams: Work closely with robotics, perception, machine learning, autonomy, simulation, and systems engineering teams to make product and technical trade-offs and ensure technical investments align with meaningful product outcomes.

Define evaluation strategy: Partner with Simulation, Systems, Engineering, and field teams to establish representative evaluation environments, test scenarios, datasets, and benchmarks for robot capability performance.

At Engine, we’re revolutionizing work travel. Our modern travel platform isn’t just about booking trips; it’s about transforming how businesses and their teams experience travel. From seamless booking with top airlines, hotels, and car rental providers to single-invoice billing and flexible trip modifications, we make travel easier to manage and better to experience.

Engine is bringing its platform to the corporate-travel channel: travel management companies (TMCs) sign on, bring their corporate accounts, and book flights, hotels, and cars on Engine, direct bill, and Flex built in. Every TMC we sign, and every corporate account behind it, has to be configured, trained, and taken through its first booking before any of that value shows up. That work is this job.

Your Mission:

As Senior Lead OBT Implementation Manager, you'll own the path from signed agreement to live, booking TMC. You'll stand each agency up on Engine (GDS credentials, agency profile, queues, agent access), configure their corporate accounts (travelers, departments, travel policies, direct bill, Flex, custom fields, rewards), train their agents, and hold the timeline across several activations at once. You'll be our first dedicated implementer, which means you define how Engine implements TMCs: you build the playbook while you run it, set the standard for the implementers who follow you, and make sure the twentieth TMC goes live in a fraction of the time the second one did.

You’ll work primarily with banks, financial institutions, and large enterprises, helping them evaluate and adopt digital asset infrastructure. You will be expected to…

greenhouse:heartflowinc:6193717004.summary: Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFR CT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFR CT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

This is a customer- facing role with a primary focus on spending time with customers including Cardiologists, Primary Care Physicians, Nurse Practitioners, and beyond. Expect approximately 20-25% travel from a home office.

Maintaining and building relationships with referring physicians and other key clinical stakeholders

greenhouse:helium10:6234875004.summary:
Pacvue is the leading Commerce Operating System, unifying retail media, commerce management, and advanced measurement across 100+ global marketplaces, including Amazon, Walmart, Target, and Instacart. Through Pacvue and Helium 10, our enterprise and SMB platforms, we empower over 70,000 brands, agencies, and sellers with AI-driven insights and technology to win in today’s rapidly evolving commerce landscape.

At Pacvue and Helium 10, great careers don’t just happen — they’re built. Here, you’ll rise as an industry leader, push the boundaries of innovation, own your journey, and thrive as part of an inclusive global community that’s redefining the future of commerce.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: We are seeking a Director of Product Management to drive execution across Helium 10’s product portfolio and to lead the product managers who deliver it. This role runs the discovery and delivery of our innovation agenda beyond the Amazon marketplace seller — into direct-to-consumer and multi-channel commerce, Walmart and TikTok, and AI-native experiences. This director will be responsible for turning agreed priorities into a sequenced, resourced roadmap and for making sure the team ships it on time and at quality.

Innovation is central to this role, and it is hands-on work. The Director of Product Management will run our new-product pipeline: validating, building, and launching the bets that open new revenue lines and new audiences. That means running structured discovery with sellers and brands, prototyping and testing quickly, defining what success looks like before we build, and retiring ideas that don’t earn their place. This leader will bring rigor to how we evaluate emerging opportunities — AI agents, autonomous workflows, and adjacent channels — and work with go-to-market teams to land them with customers.

Innovation into direct-to-consumer expansion is a core focus. As brands diversify across Shopify and their own storefronts, Google, and social commerce, our portfolio has to follow them. This director will lead the discovery, requirements, and delivery of the features that serve a DTC-first brand, and partner closely with product marketing, growth marketing, and sales to bring those products to market.

This is a hands-on, execution-first role. Sets strategy and direction for the function while also driving execution hands-on. You will run weekly operating cadences, review specs and requirements, unblock your team daily, and stay close enough to the detail to catch problems before they reach a release. The role is based in the United States and requires regular, direct contact with customers: discovery interviews, advisory sessions, and time in the field with brands and agencies. Deep familiarity with marketplace e-commerce, direct-to-consumer e-commerce, and SaaS product-led growth environments is strongly preferred.
bullets: Innovation Delivery: Run the pipeline of net-new product opportunities — from problem identification through validation, prototype, pilot, and launch. Apply a repeatable framework for evaluating bets (market size, customer evidence, technical feasibility, time to value) and the discipline to kill the ones that don’t clear the bar.

Direct-to-Consumer & Multi-Channel Expansion: Deliver the products that take Helium 10 beyond the Amazon seller — Shopify and owned storefronts, Google, Walmart, and social commerce. Review the requirements, feature priorities, and release sequencing for the DTC and omnichannel brand.

AI-Native Product Development: Identify where AI agents, generative creative, and LLM-driven workflows create real customer value rather than novelty, and build them into the roadmap with clear adoption and quality measures.

Customer Discovery: Personally lead and scale customer discovery with sellers, brands, and agencies. Build the cadence, instrumentation, and synthesis practices that keep the team’s decisions grounded in evidence instead of opinion.

Market & Competitive Intelligence: Stay ahead of market developments, platform changes, and the competitive landscape across marketplace and DTC tooling. Translate that intelligence into product decisions and executive-level point of view.

Cross-Functional Execution: Partner with engineering, design, data, and QA — organizations this role influences rather than owns — to ensure roadmap commitments ship on time and at quality. Create clarity on ownership and decision rights so work moves quickly without escalation.

Commercialization Partnership: Work with product marketing, growth, and sales on positioning, pricing, packaging, and launch readiness. Ensure every release has a defined target persona, a clear value proposition, and a plan for adoption.

Business Impact: Define success metrics for every initiative and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not outputs. Use analytics tools such as Amplitude, Tableau, and SQL to measure adoption, retention, and revenue impact, and communicate results, learnings, and recommendations to executive stakeholders.

Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.

We’re an AI company focused exclusively on heart health, building a platform that predicts and prevents cardiac events before they happen—identifying risk up to 10 days in advance versus 10 years in traditional clinical models.

This is already working at scale. Hello Heart has been shown to reduce inpatient hospital days by 47% and deliver ~$1,800 in annual savings per member. Hello Heart is the cardiac prevention partner to over 80% of large U.S. health plans and serves hundreds of public and private employers.

We’re defining how the #1 cause of death—heart disease—is managed in the AI era. Join us.

Partner with demand gen to develop and execute campaigns. You will help define the campaign vision: audience segmentation, demand hypothesis, and content topics, and working with our demand gen team help deliver sales pipeline.

Enable Sales to sell and expand. You build the tools that help revenue teams have confident conversations and partner with Sales on win/loss analysis to continuously sharpen positioning and identify gaps.

Drive post-launch adoption and expansion. CPQ is only valuable if it's adopted and used. You will work with Customer Success and Sales to identify expansion use cases, build case studies, and drive adoption campaigns that help customers realize ROI.

sections.title: You'll Have
bullets: 5+ years in marketing, with at least 3 in B2B SaaS product marketing with demonstrated experience marketing to business buyers (Sales Ops, RevOps, Finance, IT) and technical operators.

Hands-on fluency with AI tools . You use AI daily to draft, analyze, and test ideas, and you know where it fails. You can explain to a skeptical buyer where AI speeds up a quote process and where a person still needs to check the output.

Content strategy and direction chops. You've identified what assets need to exist, written the brief, set the quality bar, and coordinated subject matter experts to produce output that's both credible and compelling. You write clearly, you know what lands with business and technical audiences, and you can show the work.

Progress before the plan is finished. CPQ does not have a playbook yet. You will write the first version of the brief, make positioning calls with incomplete data, and correct course in market. You have shipped work without a process to lean on, and you can name the first three things you did when no one was there to ask.
Evidence of taking a half-built program to launch . Examples where you inherited unclear scope, defined the work yourself, and delivered results others could measure.
Experience marketing to or working alongside sales and operations professionals is a strong plus. Experience in sales tech, revenue operations, or quote-to-cash workflows is valuable.

PAX is a leading global cannabis brand redefining how people experience the plant through thoughtful design, innovative technology, and a commitment to quality. sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: PAX is seeking a Director of Product Marketing to lead product and portfolio marketing across our global device business and U.S. cannabis consumables business. They will translate consumer insight, market dynamics, and business priorities into clear portfolio strategies, differentiated product positioning, and commercially rigorous go-to-market plans.

The Director will be involved throughout the product lifecycle, from opportunity identification and product definition through commercialization, launch, and ongoing optimization. They will serve as a critical connector among Product, Marketing, Creative, Sales, E-commerce, Operations, Finance, and Insights, ensuring every product has a clear consumer proposition, role within the portfolio, and plan for commercial success. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker and strong operator who can move easily between shaping a product roadmap, refining a positioning statement, developing a global launch plan, and evaluating in-market performance.

sections.title: Shape the Portfolio
bullets: Lead product marketing across PAX’s device and consumables portfolios.
Define each product’s audience, consumer need, value proposition, and role within the broader portfolio.
Turn consumer insights, category trends, and business data into product roadmap recommendations and compelling business cases.
Help shape portfolio architecture, pricing, and lifecycle strategies across formats, markets, channels, and price points.
Translate technical information into simple, differentiated benefits that matter.

Build a deep understanding of how consumers discover, evaluate, purchase, and repurchase PAX products across channels.
Track product and launch performance across revenue, distribution, velocity, conversion, consumer response, and profitability.
Identify and lead lifecycle opportunities including pricing and promotion, bundles, product refreshes, new channel or market expansion, repositioning, and end-of-life planning.
Partner with Brand, E-commerce, Sales, and Trade Marketing to evolve messaging, content, merchandising, and demand-driving programs based on product performance and consumer behavior.
Turn performance data, competitive intelligence, and partner feedback into clear recommendations for how to accelerate, optimize, or rationalize the portfolio.
Lead post-launch and ongoing business reviews, translating insights into specific actions, owners, and success metrics.
Build repeatable processes that bring greater clarity, rigor, and accountability to how PAX launches, grows, and manages products throughout their lifecycle.

greenhouse:planetlabs:8334402.summary:
Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

As we control every component of hardware design, manufacturing, data processing, and software engineering, our office is a truly inspiring mix of experts from a variety of domains.

sections.title: Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.
paras: We have a people-centric approach toward culture and community and we strive to iterate in a way that puts our team members first and prepares our company for growth. Join Planet and be a part of our mission to change the way people see the world.
Planet is a global company with employees working remotely world wide and joining us from offices in San Francisco, Washington DC, Germany, Austria, Slovenia, and The Netherlands.

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: As a Customer Success Manager for Planet’s commercial markets, you will own our post-sale customer relationships—helping businesses integrate our satellite imagery and geospatial data into their daily workflows so they get real, measurable results from our platform.

In this role, you will manage the full customer lifecycle from onboarding through renewal and account growth. You’ll spend your time understanding how our customers' businesses actually work, anticipating what they’ll need next, and helping them prove the return on their investment in Planet. Because you'll be working with everyone from C-suite executives to technical engineers, you need to be comfortable shifting gears between high-level business strategy and technical problem-solving. You will also partner closely with our sales team, aligning your technical guidance with their commercial goals to ensure every customer has a seamless experience.
This is a full-time, hybrid role which will require you to work from our San Francisco or Denver office 3 days per week.

sections.title: Impact You'll Own:
bullets: Take full responsibility for gross and net retention across your accounts by keeping customers healthy, active, and expanding.
Partner with Account Executives to shape account strategy, bringing real customer insights and practical recommendations to your planning sessions.
Look ahead at how your customers are using Planet to catch capacity issues, churn risks, and expansion opportunities before they become urgent.
Build clear success plans and run Business Reviews that help your customers measure and show off the real business impact of Planet data.
Build strong relationships across different teams at your accounts.
Keep internal teams aligned and moving together during major account milestones, like onboarding, launches, and renewals.
Navigate high-pressure customer issues with good judgment, knowing how to prioritize and keep things on track when stakes are high.

sections.title: What You Bring:
bullets: 6+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or a similar strategic, customer-facing role.
Practical working knowledge of remote sensing, GIS, or geospatial imagery, with the ability to connect technical workflows to real business outcomes.
A track record of digging beneath surface-level requests - asking the right questions to uncover a customer's underlying goals, pressures, and business context.
A solid grasp of how commercial businesses operate (including how they make money, adapt to market shifts, and handle regulatory changes) so you can weigh the trade-offs of customer requests.
Advanced situational awareness and the ability to read a room, adjusting your tone and technical depth depending on whether you are presenting to an executive or working with a technical lead.
Clear, effective verbal and written communication skills in English, paired with a grounded presence that builds trust quickly.
Flexibility to support a global business, including availability for calls across US time zones.
Willingness to travel to meet with customers and internal teams in person.

greenhouse:procaresolutions:5476747008.summary:
For over 30 years, Procare Solutions has been dedicated to empowering early childhood educators by providing products and services that enable them to focus on the care, safety and education of children. We recognize the responsibility that comes with nurturing and educating children, which is why our child care management solutions are designed to automate business processes, help ensure safety and compliance, communicate with families and provide educational resources and training to help teachers and children thrive.

Over 40,000 satisfied customers have chosen Procare Solutions as their trusted partner in providing exceptional care for young minds.

sections.title: A Little About the Role
paras: As a Senior Customer Success Manager (CSM), you will proactively manage a dedicated portfolio of customers, building strong, long-term relationships that help the customer achieve maximum value from our solutions. This role exists to protect and grow recurring revenue within the portfolio by driving product adoption and increasing payment processing usage, directly improving key financial metrics like Gross Revenue Retention and Net Revenue Retention. Your work strengthens customer loyalty and retention and delivers on measurable, lasting value to their assigned accounts.

sections.title: What you’ll do:
bullets: Proactive Customer Engagement: Strengthen and broaden key customer relationships through regular contact, acting as a trusted advisor and proactively identifying and assisting in the timely resolution of customer issues.

Value Realization: Create and execute tailored Customer Success Plans (CSPs) for each account, outlining specific goals, milestones, and metrics for driving product adoption, increasing payment processing, and demonstrating ROI.

Performance & Health Monitoring: Regularly monitor account health and usage data to identify at-risk customers and opportunities for growth, and take proactive measures to mitigate risks and ensure customer satisfaction.

Continuous Improvement: Collect and relay customer feedback to internal teams (e.g., Product, Engineering, Marketing) to help improve offerings and overall customer experience.
Innovation: Develop and refine frameworks and methodologies for Customer Success, defining how we engaged with and grow our most important customers.

sections.title: Our ideal candidate will have:

Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and persuasively at an executive level.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.

Use of computer, telephone, and other office equipment for the greater part of the workday

greenhouse:prolific:5033054101.summary:
Prolific isn’t just enabling AI innovation – we’re redefining it. While foundational AI technologies are becoming commoditized, Prolific’s human data infrastructure provides the high-quality, diverse data required to train the next generation of AI models. Through our platform, we empower researchers and companies to access a global, ethically curated participant base, ensuring cutting-edge AI research and training grounded in inclusivity and precision.

T his is a brand new role, and you’ll be the first person to do it at Prolific.

Right now, the insight that could help us win more deals is scattered. We have valuable learnings about why we win, why we lose, and why deals stall, but they aren’t turned into the pitch, proof and materials that sellers use every day. You’ll fix that. You’ll become the person who knows our market position inside out and turns it into tools that help…

sections.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager, Sales Enablement (AI & Research)
paras: You’ll be measured on win rate, sales cycle length, rep ramp time and how well equipped our sellers are in front of a buyer.

Our AI PMM leads strategic lab and enterprise AI pursuits, and our vertical PMMs tailor messaging for specific audiences. You own the foundation they all build on: the shared, trusted system of resources every other deal runs on.

We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
bullets: 6+ years in an enablement-facing role (product marketing, sales enablement or competitive intelligence) at a B2B company
Experience enabling sellers across more than one product or product line, at a startup, scale-up or enterprise
Experience doing the full job, not just the final slides: you’ve gathered the data and insight yourself, then turned it into materials sellers use
Enablement you’ve built that measurably moved win rate, ramp time or deal velocity. You can show who used it and what changed

Comfort with data: you can pull from a CRM and call-intelligence tools, build an analysis or business case, and defend your conclusions
Clear writing for busy readers: short, specific and easy to act on
Credibility with sellers and senior leaders, and the ability to get sales, product and customer success to act without managing any of them. You’ll spend a lot of time with sales

greenhouse:protonai:6190963004.summary:
Proton is building the AI operating system for wholesale distribution, embedded in the workflows that move nearly every physical product on the planet. Distribution is a $9 trillion industry running on software that has been stuck for decades. We unify CRM, PIM, eCommerce AI, and Order & Quote Entry AI into one platform with one data layer and one AI brain, so reps spend their time on customer relationships instead of data entry.

We have been building AI into distribution since 2018, long before it became an industry buzzword. That head start matters, and we've only deepened the investment: in 2025 we shipped the first AI assistant embedded in a distribution CRM and launched a complete agentic product in our PIM offering.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to own product domains end to end. Reporting to the VP of Product, you'll lead a multi-functional squad at the intersection of AI capability and real distributor workflows, turning our positioning advantage into compounding product differentiation.

End to end means further than it usually does. You inherit a problem space rather than a backlog: work out where the real value sits across hundreds of distributors, ship in tight cycles with design partners keeping you honest, prove the thing works in production, then drive adoption across the base and make it something sales can sell without you. There is no handoff point where the domain stops being yours.
Location: Cambridge, MA. Hybrid, 3 days a week in our Harvard Square office.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own your domain from fuzzy to growth. Take an ambiguous problem space through discovery, definition, build, launch, adoption, and revenue. You are responsible for the outcome.

Get onsite, constantly. Distributors work in warehouses and on sales floors. Onsite visits, shadowing sessions, and discovery calls are how you learn the domain, and the best calls come from standing next to a rep. Our product people know their users by name.

Run genuinely iterative development with customers in the loop. Think big, ship small, put working software in front of real users early, and let what you learn reset the next cycle. Design the feedback loop deliberately rather than waiting for feedback to arrive.
Build hands-on with engineering, design, and data science to ship features and agentic workflows, and to make sure the surrounding UX lets a user act on what AI surfaces.
Own adoption, not just launch. Run alphas and betas, stay close through the first rollouts, then push adoption across the installed base and watch where it stalls and why.

Enable GTM. Give sales and CS the positioning, proof, and training they need. Join customer and prospect calls, show the product yourself when it helps, and make sure what you built is sellable and supportable without you in the room.

sections.title: What You'll Need to Succeed
bullets: Product and startup experience. At least 2 years managing features end-to-end through the SDLC. Early-stage startup experience (Seed through B or C) is a plus.

Real agile experience, and the judgment to adapt it. You've worked inside traditional scrum, know what those rituals were for, and can run a tight iterative loop with customers rather than a release calendar. You've shipped something incomplete on purpose because it was the fastest way to learn.

Technical and AI collaboration. You've built alongside engineers and data scientists to deploy AI-centric features at scale, and you're fluent enough to hold your own with senior engineers on data models, APIs, and service boundaries.

Daily, hands-on use of AI in your own practice. Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent, used to ship real work rather than generate artifacts. You can say concretely how you structure context and how you check what comes back.

Customer-facing range. You're as comfortable in a warehouse aisle with a rep as on a call with a VP of Sales, and you can carry a room in front of a prospect. You'd rather be with a user than briefed about them.
Data-driven and adaptive thinking. You make data-driven calls while embracing the uncertainty earlier-stage vertical B2B SaaS brings.
Problem-solving and communication. You navigate complexity, distill the key issue, and communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
Business sense and a continuous improvement mindset. Strong business intuition and a real appetite for innovation, iteration, and AI excellence.

sections.title: Big Plus
bullets: Complex B2B, enterprise, or ERP-adjacent software, with high-frequency users and workflows people can't opt out of.
Agentic products, and the patterns for trust, correction, and handoff between a person and an agent.
Systems-of-record or integrations work. You understand how messy real-world source data becomes a clean, canonical model, and what breaks when it doesn't.

Proton is building the AI operating system for wholesale distribution, embedded in the workflows that move nearly every physical product on the planet. Distribution is a $9 trillion industry running on software that has been stuck for decades. sections.title: The Role
paras: We're hiring an Implementation Manager to own standard customer engagements from pre-sales solutioning through a successful go-live. As part of Forward Deployed Engineering, you'll be the customer-facing owner of the plan, the work, and the outcome—translating real distributor workflows into an implementation that delivers value quickly and sticks.

Implementation here means more than a handoff after a deal closes. You'll help Sales shape a workable solution before signature, define scope and success criteria, lead the project through configuration, integrations, data, testing, training, and go-live, then leave the customer set up to run on Proton. You'll act as the engagement lead for standard implementations: equally comfortable driving details, aligning senior stakeholders, and surfacing what needs to change. You'll partner with Engineering and Engagement Managers when scope, technical risk, or stakeholder complexity exceeds the standard path. This role is designed as a growth path into an Engagement Manager role driving complex customer engagements.
Location: Cambridge, MA. Hybrid, 3 days a week in our Harvard Square office.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Partner in pre-sales solutioning. Join discovery and solution-design conversations, turn requirements into clear scopes and phased plans, surface dependencies and risks early, and make sure what is sold can be implemented well.

Lead the delivery plan. Take each project from signed agreement through go-live: kickoff, project plan, configuration, integrations, data readiness, testing, training, and cutover. Keep every workstream moving and every owner clear.

Run stakeholder governance and risk. Establish the right cadence with customer champions, technical teams, and executives. Keep decisions and risks visible, escalate early when a plan needs to change, and resolve issues before they become surprises.

Translate business workflows into a technical plan. Get close to how a distributor sells, quotes, manages products, and enters orders; then work with customers and Proton teammates to configure the right workflow, data model, and integration approach.

Drive integration and data work with good judgment. You do not need to be the engineer writing every integration, but you can assess API, source-system, data-quality, and integration risks well enough to make tradeoffs visible and bring in the right technical owner.

Make go-live real. Define acceptance criteria, lead UAT and readiness reviews, prepare users for change, coordinate cutover, and stay close enough after launch to ensure the new workflow is actually adopted.
Own implementation outcomes. Track time to value, on-time go-lives, activation, implementation CSAT, and project health. Forecast risk honestly and act early when a plan needs to change.

Build the repeatable motion. Turn lessons from customers into sharper playbooks, templates, estimates, product feedback, and sales enablement. Help make each normal implementation faster, clearer, and better than the last.

sections.title: What You'll Need to Succeed
bullets: Implementation and project-management experience. 2+ years in implementation, technical project delivery, professional services, or a comparable role, with demonstrated ownership of customer outcomes. Early-stage B2B SaaS experience is a plus.

Technical fluency. You can work productively with APIs, integrations, data models, source systems, and configuration. You ask precise questions, identify risk, and can hold your own with customer technical teams and senior engineers.

Pre-sales judgment. You can turn ambiguous customer needs into an implementable plan, distinguish a requirement from a nice-to-have, surface constraints without creating friction, and protect the path to value.

Excellent execution under real-world constraints. You know how to build and run a project plan, coordinate dependencies, make decisions visible, and move multiple workstreams forward without losing the detail.

Customer-facing range. You're as comfortable in a warehouse aisle with an operations team as you are running a meeting with senior stakeholders. You'd rather understand the work firsthand than manage by secondhand notes.
Clear communication and calm ownership. You can explain technical tradeoffs in plain language, earn trust quickly, and keep customers and internal teams aligned when things are messy.

Practical use of AI in your own work. You regularly use AI tools to accelerate planning, analysis, documentation, and coordination, and know how to provide context, evaluate outputs, and correct mistakes.
Data-driven and adaptive thinking. You use project and customer data to decide what needs attention, while staying flexible as details change.

sections.title: Big Plus
bullets: Complex B2B, enterprise, or ERP-adjacent software, with high-frequency users and operational workflows people can't opt out of.
Wholesale distribution, manufacturing, logistics, or another operationally complex industry.
CRM, PIM, eCommerce, order management, or systems-of-record integrations.
Experience delivering AI-enabled workflows in a customer environment, including the trust, correction, and handoff patterns that make them useful.

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL DO
bullets: Champion Strategic Portfolio Vision: Define and drive the long-term vision and technical roadmap for enterprise object storage, identifying emerging architectural patterns and customer requirements to establish enduring product differentiation.

Guide End-to-End Product Architecture: Direct the full product lifecycle from incubation to global release, establishing rigorous performance, scalability, and durability benchmarks that maximize customer value and drive sustained portfolio adoption.

Cultivate Global Customer & Ecosystem Alliances: Partner with Global Sales, Systems Engineering, and top technology alliance partners to shape technical go-to-market strategies, serving as a trusted technical advisor and spokesperson for enterprise customers worldwide.

Advise Cross-Functional & Executive Leadership: Synthesize industry trends, regulatory changes, and competitive landscapes into clear business priorities, collaborating across Core Systems Engineering and executive teams to guide high-impact investment decisions.

sections.title: WHAT YOU BRING
paras: This range is our good faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to pay for this position upon hire, as of the date of this posting. lever:crypto:f66cc817-371b-469c-8bc8-52a.summary:
We are looking for a Senior/Principal Product Manager to own customer onboarding across the Crypto.com App and adjacent product surfaces. Onboarding is where regulatory requirements, customer acquisition, and time-to-first-value meet. Every improvement you ship should help more customers open an account compliantly, activate faster, and reach the products that matter.

Your mandate is to own the onboarding journey as both a growth product and a regulated platform: KYC and account opening, activation and referral mechanics, new-product onboarding, and a meaningful trading scope. Within six months, you will own the onboarding-and-growth charter and take on trading product work in addition to the onboarding charter.

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: You will report to Onboarding squad Lead and work closely on the trading portion of the charter. You will run your roadmap with independence, make prioritization calls, and own the how and the when.

If you have built onboarding in a regulated consumer fintech, parts of this will feel familiar. The difference is the breadth: one onboarding platform must support a growing set of products, regulatory paths, and trading journeys. The playbook is still being written.

sections.title: What You'll Actually Do:
bullets: Own compliant customer onboarding end-to-end. You set the roadmap for account opening, identity verification, KYC requirements, and platform capabilities. You make the tradeoffs between conversion, speed, risk, and regulatory obligations.

Turn onboarding into a growth engine. You own activation, referral, new-user incentives, and time-to-first-value. You partner with Marketing on acquisition mechanics and remain accountable for what happens after the click.

Instrument and improve the funnel. You identify where customers drop, size the opportunity, ship interventions, and measure whether completion and activation move. You do not wait for someone else to hand you the analysis.

Extend the platform across products. You take onboarding capabilities built for the Main App and adapt them for other platforms and future product surfaces without creating fragmented journeys or one-off systems.

Own a meaningful trading slice. You pick up trading-product work alongside Trading team and connect onboarding to first trade and continued participation. You do not need to be the specialist, but you must be able to hold the trading product conversation.

Lead across functions without hiding behind escalation. You align Engineering, Design, Compliance, Marketing, and Trading around priorities, dependencies, and launch decisions. When regulation or delivery constraints change, you re-plan and keep the outcome intact.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: You have owned consumer onboarding and growth together. You can point to an activation, referral, acquisition, or time-to-value problem you owned, the intervention you shipped, and the number that moved.

You have shipped account opening or KYC in a regulated product. You can describe how identity, country rules, or a regulatory change affected the funnel-and what you changed without treating compliance as a black box.
You have extended a shared onboarding capability across products or markets. You can explain how you reused the platform while adapting the journey to a new product, brand, or regulatory context.

You have enough trading-product depth to take ownership. You have owned or worked deeply on a trading, brokerage, investing, or first-trade journey and can discuss the customer, mechanics, and tradeoffs without coaching.

You operate as a senior individual contributor. You can run two connected charters, make prioritization calls, and ship through ambiguity without needing a manager to structure every decision. We care what you have built and owned-not pedigree or a fixed number of years.

sections.title: Preferred:
bullets: Crypto trading: You have worked on a consumer crypto product and can ramp quickly into Crypto.com’s trading journeys.

lever:truv:8e04c5ba-c4be-406d-b8eb-dad5b.summary:
Truv is building the infrastructure layer that powers consumer-permissioned income, employment, identity, and asset verification. We help lenders, fintechs, and financial institutions make faster, more accurate decisions while delivering a seamless consumer experience.

As we continue to expand our data network and verification capabilities, we're looking for a Lead Product Manager to own and scale our Data Sources platform—the foundation that powers document ingestion, fraud detection, bank connectivity, and data reliability across Truv products.

sections.title: About the Job:
paras: We are seeking an experienced Lead Product Manager, Data Sources to own the execution of the roadmap, and execution for the systems that collect, process, and validate consumer financial data.

This role sits at the intersection of data infrastructure, machine learning, fraud prevention, and financial data aggregation. You will be responsible for building scalable capabilities that improve data coverage, quality, reliability, and trust across Truv's platform.

You will work closely with Engineering, Data Science, Fraud, Operations, Customer Success, and GTM teams to deliver products that directly impact conversion, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency.

sections.title: What You'll Own:
paras: Document parsing - Drive the roadmap for parsing income and document types. Improve accuracy, reduce manual review, and shorten time-to-report. Partner with Data Science on extraction models and with Ops on the human-in-the-loop pipeline.

Scaling document types - Expand the catalog of supported document types beyond the current set. Identify the highest-impact additions (by use case, client demand, and revenue impact), prioritize the rollout, and own the end-to-end product surface from upload to verified output.

Fraud detection - Define and ship the fraud signal layer across data sources — document tampering detection, deposit-pattern anomalies, identity mismatches, and synthetic income flags. Balance precision and recall against client-specific risk tolerances, and build the configuration surface for clients to tune.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Set the multi-quarter roadmap for Data Sources across docs, fraud, and aggregation; align it with revenue, client commitments, and platform-level constraints.
Write tight specs and 1-pagers; partner with Eng and Data Science to scope, build, and ship.
Talk to clients (mortgage lenders, government agencies, tenant screeners) weekly; turn their feedback into prioritized roadmap.
Own the metrics — parse accuracy, fraud catch rate, bank connection success, SLA hit rate — and the rituals that drive them up.
Lead and mentor PMs and engineers on the team; raise the bar on shipping speed and quality.
Represent Truv's data sources story externally (sales calls, conferences, partner reviews).

sections.title: Who You Are
bullets: 7+ years in product management , with significant time in data, ML/AI, fintech, or verification / identity platforms.
Demonstrated experience owning a data-intensive product — document understanding, OCR, financial data aggregation, fraud, or similar — at meaningful scale.
Strong technical fluency. You can reason about extraction models, API tradeoffs, and pipeline architecture without needing to be hand-held by engineering.
Track record of driving SLA / reliability outcomes — not just shipping features, but moving the numbers that matter.
Experience working with regulated industries (mortgage, lending, government) is a strong plus. GSE / FCRA / FNMA / FHLMC familiarity especially.
Strong written communication. You write the 1-pagers and specs that align the team.
Customer obsession. You spend real time with users and let what you learn shape the roadmap.
Worked on a verification or KYC/KYB product used by lenders.

recruitee:vesper:2725039.summary:
We built and scaled a global customer base from our headquarters in Amsterdam. The United States became one of our most important markets, so we put people on the ground here. Our Chicago office in River North is open and running.

You'd be joining early, but not from zero. The person who built and ran our European mid-market sales team has moved to Chicago. We have an experienced Account Management team in Amsterdam, and you’ll onboard with them to learn every hard-won lesson from scaling that business: how customers actually get value from the platform, which conversations lead to expansion, how renewals are won long before they're due. Our first U.S. SDR is here, ramped and hitting their numbers. An Account Executive is closing new business alongside you. And one of our product marketers sits in this office, giving you a direct line into the product team when a customer needs…

sections.title: About the role
paras: We've also been increasing investment in our marketing channels month over month, which means a growing customer base in North America for you to build on.

The timing couldn't be better. For years, FMCG companies have been stuck with limited choice among legacy market intelligence providers. Every quarter, more of them switch to Vesper. Once they do, the opportunity is to make Vesper indispensable to how they buy. That's your job. And you'll get to visit the canals in Amsterdam from time to time to meet the rest of your colleagues in person.

T his is not your typical account management role. There's no queue of tickets and no script. You'll be the CEO of your portfolio: responsible for whether customers succeed with Vesper, whether they renew, and how much they grow.

sections.title: Why you should join us
bullets: Own your portfolio outright. You decide where your time goes, which accounts to invest in, and how to grow them. Real responsibility, no hand-holding.
Retention and expansion, not just check-ins. You'll carry a number for both. The best account managers here find revenue that nobody asked them to find.
Sell to the toughest audience there is. Procurement teams negotiate for a living. Renewing and expanding with them is one of the best commercial educations you can get.

The European playbook is in the building. The leader who scaled our mid-market business in Europe is now based in Chicago, and a Vesper product marketer sits here too, so customer patterns, product answers, and proven approaches are a desk away rather than an eight-hour time difference.

Shape how we do this in North America. You're senior enough that the way you run onboarding, business reviews, and renewals becomes the pattern the next hires follow. You'll help define the North American customer motion, not inherit it.
We invest in your growth. We bring in outside trainers, run the internal Vesper Academy, and coach you on negotiation, commercial conversations, and account strategy.
Face-to-face, not just video. You'll visit strategic accounts across North America and represent Vesper at trade shows and industry events.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
bullets: Own the full post-sale lifecycle. Onboarding, adoption, renewal, expansion. You manage all of it, proactively, for your book of North American accounts.
Grow your portfolio. Understand your customers' workflows deeply enough to find expansion opportunities before they surface as requests, then build the business case and close them.
Protect and win renewals. Know where every account stands well ahead of the date, negotiate value rather than discount, and forecast your book honestly.

Make customers demonstrably better at their jobs. You don't need to be a commodity consultant, but you do need to know the platform inside out and how each customer can extract the most value from it based on what they're actually trying to achieve.

Keep Vesper essential. Make sure customers know what the platform can do, stay current on new releases, and treat Vesper as a fixture in their workflow rather than a subscription they review once a year.
Feed the roadmap. Ask the right questions, listen, and get real customer signal back to our product team. With a product marketer down the hall, that loop is short.
Set the standard. As the first local Account Manager, you'll help build the playbook for North American account management and support newer team members as we grow the office.

sections.title: What you'll bring
paras: The role can be a Senior Account Manager for candidates with the right experience.
bullets: 4+ years owning customer relationships commercially, whether as an Account Manager, Customer Success Manager, or Account Executive in technology, or a background in procurement or trading that you've since turned commercial. Roughly four years plus, but experience matters more than the count.
A track record of carrying and hitting a retention or expansion number

A strong commercial mindset. What we mean by that: you understand how your customers' businesses work and how they make money, you've negotiated value before, and you actually enjoy the idea of selling something.
Genuine curiosity about customer workflows, and the discipline to turn what you learn into adoption and revenue
Comfort using data to decide where your attention goes
A natural team player. You contribute to the team's target, not just your own, and support the people around you.
Comfortable in a fast-paced environment where some processes exist and others you'll build; you learn quickly and adapt as our proposition evolves
Excellent written and spoken English. Spanish or French is a plus

smartrecruiters:achieve1:374399001701383.summary:
As Director of Product Management for Achieve Debt Optimizer*, you will own the company's next-generation consumer debt product end to end. Achieve Debt Optimizer*evaluates a consumer's whole debt picture and matches them to the right solution across Achieve and partner products, loan and non-loan alike. It is not a budgeting app and not a single-product lender.

This is a core product leadership role with two amplified mandates: building the partner ecosystem that powers the marketplace and taking the product to market. You will turn a validated zero-to-one concept into a scaled, monetized platform heading into 2027. Achieve Debt Optimizer* is a strategic initiative anchoring the company's long-term growth objective. It runs a decoupled front end and back end, and its roadmap evolves on transitioning from single product solutions into multi product bundles that include multiyear debt…

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: Lead the product from validated prototype to scaled platform: define requirements, sequence releases and make clear trade-offs across scope, speed and risk.
Define the decisioning experience: whole-portfolio debt evaluation, Fit Score and account-level ratings, Smart Move recommendations, bundling logic and liability drag.
Partner with design and research to run rapid concept tests and turn findings into product decisions.
Shape AI-enabled and agentic experiences, including the conversational navigator, so they lift conversion and consumer trust.

Build the partner strategy for loan and non-loan solutions and partnerships: partner with BD to identify, prioritize and onboard partners across refinance, auto and student lending, balance transfer, credit counseling and other external solutions.
Own the partner API and integration product: pre-qualification and pricing exchange, eligibility, offer return, attribution and reporting.
Define partner onboarding, certification and performance standards; manage the integration pipeline with Partner B2B and Engineering.
Design marketplace economics with Finance and Partnerships: revenue share, lead and funded-loan monetization, and partner-level reporting.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: 10+ years in product management, with hands-on experience.
A track record of taking a zero-to-one consumer product to scale and owning its P&L or revenue outcomes.
Experience building marketplace or platform products with third-party partners: partner APIs, integrations, offer exchange and partner economics.
Hands-on go-to-market leadership: positioning, pricing and packaging, launch, and channel strategy with Marketing and Sales.
Consumer-facing experience and strong understanding in experimentation.
Strong analytical skills: funnel and unit-economics fluency, experiment design and data-driven prioritization.
Executive presence and the ability to align senior leaders, partners and cross-functional teams around a clear direction.
Experience with lending marketplaces, loan-matching or offer-aggregation platforms.

sections.title: Who you'll work with
paras: You'll work directly with senior executives to shape and pressure-test product direction. You'll also work cross functionally with Design, Research, Engineering, Marketing, BD and Legal & Compliance.
This is a high-autonomy, high-impact role for a leader who is hands-on that thrives in ambiguity, moves fast and wants to define a new category in consumer debt.

sections.title: The Impact You'll Make
paras: Your work will directly reshape how millions of people find financial freedom and think about debt. You'll define the experience that power the company's core growth engine. You'll measure success by how many people you empower to take control of their financial future—and by how much you help Achieve grow sustainably and responsibly.

This role sits on the Digital Experiences team and will help shape product strategy, build business cases, align senior leaders around investment decisions, bring new 0-to-1 opportunities to market, and grow established platforms into larger digital businesses.

The Product Manager will own and develop digital opportunities that create value for Mattel beyond one-time campaign activations. This includes fan engagement products, physical-to-digital extensions, collector utilities, subscription or service concepts, cross-brand digital platforms, and reusable experience infrastructure. The role requires strong product judgment, comfort with ambiguity, disciplined execution,…

sections.title: The Opportunity:

sections.title: What Your Impact Will Be:

Build product strategies and business cases that clarify the audience opportunity, consumer value proposition, revenue model, investment needs, risks, dependencies, and path to scale.
Partner with Digital Experiences leadership to align ELT and senior stakeholders around strategic priorities, funding asks, investment tradeoffs, and launch decisions.
Own established digital platforms and identify opportunities to improve engagement, retention, monetization, operating efficiency, and long-term scalability.
Translate business goals, audience needs, and brand strategies into clear product requirements, roadmaps, briefs, user stories, success metrics, and decision frameworks.
Evaluate opportunities based on audience value, business impact, feasibility, scalability, monetization potential, first-party data value, and reusable capability.
Help shift digital work from one-time launches toward living products that are measured, maintained, improved, and scaled over time.

sections.title: What We’re Looking For:
bullets: 5+ years of product management experience building consumer-facing digital products, apps, platforms, services, ecommerce experiences, fan communities, subscriptions, or other digital experiences.

Demonstrated success taking digital products from concept through launch and post-launch growth, with clear examples of business impact, user adoption, engagement, retention, monetization, or operational improvement.

Strong product strategy skills, including the ability to define customer problems, size opportunities, shape MVPs, prioritize tradeoffs, create roadmaps, and make clear recommendations with incomplete information.

Strong analytical judgment, including the ability to define success metrics, interpret product performance, identify actionable insights, and recommend whether to scale, optimize, pivot, pause, or sunset an initiative.
Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to align creative, technical, business, and brand stakeholders.
Strong execution discipline, including planning, dependency management, vendor coordination, launch readiness, risk tracking, and follow-through.

bullets: Experience in entertainment, consumer products, kids/family products, digital media, subscriptions, DTC, fan platforms, or branded digital experiences.
Experience working with licensed or franchise-based IP.
Familiarity with app stores, web products, live operations, user acquisition, CRM, community, content platforms, or digital commerce.
Experience using product analytics tools, A/B testing, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, or lifecycle metrics.
